Playbook.name: Windows — Remote-Execution Service Installed on a New Host (PsExec / PAExec / RemCom Family) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A remote-execution service (PSEXESVC, PAExec, RemCom, CSExec, winexesvc, impacket, SecretsDump) was installed (7045) on a host first-seen for it (new_terms). Triage question: is this lateral movement/credential dumping, or an admin using PsExec legitimately on a new host?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: These service names are the fingerprints of remote-execution and credential-dumping tools; installation on a new host signals lateral movement.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: Remote-exec service install
Signal.Details: 7045 with a PsExec/PAExec/RemCom/Impacket/SecretsDump service name, new host.

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Host where the service was installed.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the remote-execution service install is lateral movement/credential dumping or legitimate admin use.

Step.name: Service install detail and any SecretsDump indicator
Step.Purpose: The service name and image path reveal the tool; SecretsDump/impacket names indicate credential theft, not just execution.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.system-* | WHERE event.code == "7045" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, winlog.event_data.ServiceName, winlog.event_data.ImagePath, winlog.event_data.ServiceType, winlog.event_data.AccountName | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: SecretsDump*/impacket* = credential dumping (worse than plain PsExec). ImagePath with a random name in ADMIN$/temp = attacker tool. A one-off admin PsExec differs from a sweep.

Step.name: Broader spread - same service family on other hosts
Step.Purpose: The same remote-exec service appearing on multiple hosts is active lateral movement.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.system-* | WHERE event.code == "7045" AND winlog.event_data.ServiceName RLIKE "(?i)(psexe|paexec|remcom|csexec|winexe|impacket|secretsdump|btobto).*" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS installs = COUNT(*), hosts = COUNT_DISTINCT(host.name), host_list = VALUES(host.name), services = VALUES(winlog.event_data.ServiceName) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: Multiple hosts with the same remote-exec service family in the window = lateral movement campaign - escalate. One host may be a single admin action.

Node.Condition: SecretsDump/impacket service (credential dumping), or the same remote-exec service across multiple hosts.
Node.Result: True Positive (Lateral Movement / Credential Dumping - IR)

Node.Condition: A single PSEXESVC install by a documented admin performing a known remote task.
Remote-exec service install with unclear admin provenance.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-REMSVC-INSTALL, INV-02-REMSVC-SPREAD to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: A sanctioned admin using PsExec for a known task.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the task; close as benign_activity; new_terms will learn the host.

TruePositive.Definition: Lateral movement or credential dumping via remote-execution tooling.

Indicators.Item: Random image path in admin share/temp.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate affected hosts; open IR; treat credentials on them as exposed.
Scope the spread; reset exposed credentials.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A management tool using an embedded PsExec-like service by design.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
